one_line: Agent-assisted appointment search, comparison, reservation, and monitoring.
what_it_does: Simulated marketplace where an agent filters and ranks appointment slots, asks for human approval, reserves, or keeps watching for a match.
leverage_rationale: Shared live state and a keep-watching workflow make structured agent operation materially more reliable than repeatedly driving a UI, although the underlying marketplace outcome is still achievable through browser automation.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies shared app state for UI and tools.
Flow includes search, compare, approve, reserve and persistent keep_watching/check_watch states.
execution_rationale: The described flow is coherent and the live demo/repository are reported alive, but there is no submitted video and the Devpost media panel was inaccessible in the screenshot, so end-to-end completion is only claimed.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and a public repository is listed.
Screenshot shows QueueLess packaging but embedded content reports a connection-security restriction.
No video frame sheets submitted.
impact_rationale: Appointment availability is a concrete, recurring user problem; delegating monitoring while preserving approval has credible value for people competing for scarce slots.
impact_evidence: Pitch addresses refresh-heavy appointment hunting.
Human approval is required before reservation.
creativity_rationale: Keep Watching with an agent waiting for inventory is a fresh, memorable extension of appointment search, though the marketplace category itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Persistent agent monitoring is central to the stated concept.
The product frames the workflow around only returning when a decision is needed.
usability_note: The stated search-to-approval flow is understandable; inaccessible embedded media limits observed usability.
red_flags: Simulated inventory and no end-to-end video evidence.
Embedded Devpost media was inaccessible in the screenshot.
standouts: Keep Watching turns agent attention into an explicit product capability.
advance_reason: Strong use case and meaningful WebMCP delta, with execution evidence limited by absent video.

one_line: Mission control where agents propose lifecycle moves and humans approve verified changes.
what_it_does: Agents inspect tasks, dependencies, evidence, and revisions, then create proposal-only actions; a human revalidates and approves lifecycle changes.
leverage_rationale: The structured shared state, proposal queue, evidence gate, revision check, and audit trail are the product's core collaboration model and are difficult to reproduce comparably through pixel-oriented automation.
leverage_evidence: Eight imperative tools share live task, evidence, proposal, approval, and audit state.
Agent cannot approve; human approval rechecks revision and completion evidence.
Contact sheet visibly states Agent proposes, Human decides, Mission Center verifies.
execution_rationale: Surfaces and stated workflow align coherently, and the contact sheet shows repeated mission-control states and human-in-command stages; lack of transcript and limited packaging reduce certainty of actual completion.
execution_evidence: Contact sheet shows mission workflow UI with proposal, decision, and verification states.
Deterministic Node tests and verification scripts are claimed.
Demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Teams operating consequential tasks need auditable agent assistance without surrendering authority; the evidence/revision gate directly addresses that need.
impact_evidence: Defined task-review audience and lifecycle workflow.
Proposal-only mutations and auditability address operational safety.
creativity_rationale: The explicit separation of agent proposal, human authority, and verification is a thoughtful interaction model beyond a generic agent dashboard.
creativity_evidence: Human-in-command workflow is encoded as product state, not merely a policy statement.
Mission Center revalidates evidence before the final transition.
usability_note: The contact sheet suggests a legible staged workflow, though detailed interaction cannot be confirmed from packaging alone.
red_flags: Submission discloses derivation from an existing Codex Mission Center project.
No public repository and no transcript.
standouts: Clear separation of proposal and authority.
advance_reason: One of the clearest structured human-agent control patterns, with strong leverage and coherent visual evidence.

one_line: Browser-local construction schedule editor operated by an agent through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Edits ADM network schedules, calculates CPM/float and critical path locally, and lets an agent inspect and shift activities without exporting sensitive schedule data.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to a large dependency graph plus local recalculation and privacy preservation creates a major capability beyond generic UI driving, especially where schedule data cannot leave the browser.
leverage_evidence: IndexedDB-local schedule and client-side CPM calculations are described.
Agent reads float and shifts activities with ripple recalculation.
Contact sheets show schedule/network editor states and agent-operable controls.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a specific editor, loaded schedule, dependency calculations, and live demo; frame sheets provide product-motion evidence, though no transcript confirms every claimed path.
execution_evidence: Three submitted video frame sheets show the construction schedule interface.
Demo is reported alive with a real schedule loaded.
Public repository and two gallery images are listed.
impact_rationale: Construction planners have a real need to reason about dependency and float changes while protecting sensitive project schedules; the local architecture fits that constraint.
impact_evidence: Specific construction scheduling audience and ADM/CPM workflow.
Privacy rationale ties local processing to industry sensitivity.
creativity_rationale: Applying browser-native agent operation to Japanese ADM construction scheduling, with privacy as a first-class constraint, is an unusually specific and ambitious concept.
creativity_evidence: Nonstandard arrow-diagram scheduling domain.
Agent-driven ripple effects through a dependency network are central.
usability_note: A loaded schedule and concrete operations reduce setup friction, but the specialized graph may be demanding for new users.
red_flags: No transcript and no direct observed tool call in the packet.
Highly specialized domain may narrow initial users.
advance_reason: High leverage, strong domain fit, and credible visual evidence of a specialized working product.

one_line: Natural-language decision engine for selecting food, grocery, and service options.
what_it_does: Uses simulated example data and user requirements to rank three options, explain tradeoffs, support what-if budget changes, and route toward confirmation/payment.
leverage_rationale: Natural-language multi-criteria selection benefits from structured tools, but the described result could largely be obtained by a general agent operating the interface.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes category selection, chat/voice/image input, ranked options, and what-if simulation.
All simulations are explicitly example-data based.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a broad multi-step flow, but evidence is packaging-only with no video sheets and simulated data; completeness of payment and confirmation is not demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Screenshot is a Devpost packaging page with gallery imagery listed in facts.
About text states example data only.
No video frame sheets submitted.
impact_rationale: Choosing among food, grocery, and service options is a recognizable need, but simulated data and unclear real-world completion weaken demonstrated value.
impact_evidence: Three concrete consumer categories and budget what-if behavior are described.
No real data is used.
creativity_rationale: The compromise-ranking and what-if framing add a useful angle to recommendation, but the overall decision-engine category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Best-three compromise recommendations with explanations.
Budget adjustment for no-fit cases.
usability_note: The stated flow is understandable but broad and includes several confirmation/payment transitions that are not evidenced.
red_flags: Example data only.
No video evidence.
Scope spans recommendation through payment without end-to-end proof.
standouts: Explicit tradeoff explanations and what-if budgeting.
advance_reason: Recognizable concept but thin execution and WebMCP evidence compared with stronger packets.

one_line: Invoice-review assistant that stages evidence-backed decisions for human approval.
what_it_does: Reads a payable queue, exposes exact variance and permitted actions, and stages a visible credit-and-hold draft without releasing payment or contacting suppliers.
leverage_rationale: Structured queue/evidence access and constrained proposal mutation materially improve reliable review while preserving a hard human decision boundary.
leverage_evidence: Two WebMCP tools return run, source IDs, exact variance, allowed actions, and status.
Agent cannot confirm, release payment, or contact supplier.
Frame sheets show invoice evidence, $200 hold, and Agent Draft states.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a narrow, internally consistent workflow and the frame sheets visibly cover queue, variance evidence, and draft staging; final human decision is intentionally outside agent scope.
execution_evidence: Three video frame sheets show product states.
Specific PP-2086 discrepancy is eight units at $119 versus $94, totaling $200.
Demo and public repository are reported alive.
impact_rationale: Accounts-payable reviewers have a real costly error-detection problem, and evidence-backed staging can save time without automating the high-risk payment decision.
impact_evidence: Concrete invoice exception and deterministic variance.
Human confirms or dismisses the staged resolution.
creativity_rationale: The concept is a strong, safety-conscious synthesis of invoice automation and WebMCP proposal semantics, though payable review is an established category.
creativity_evidence: Deterministic checks are explicitly separate from agent action.
Visible Agent Draft is constrained to permitted choices.
usability_note: Small tool surface and explicit evidence/draft boundary should be easy to understand.
red_flags: Fictional invoice packets.
Video does not appear to demonstrate a real external payment integration.
standouts: Excellent safety boundary and evidence specificity.
advance_reason: Strong execution and practical impact with meaningful WebMCP leverage.

one_line: Shared rooms where agents get computers, tool calls become commits, and humans approve irreversible work.
what_it_does: Coordinates multiple agents and human roles, shared logs, per-agent Linux computers, staged drafts, approved tool expansion, and publish queues with human-only approval.
leverage_rationale: Shared agent-human state, role-scoped credentials, per-agent computers, live tool registry propagation, and commit-like receipts define capabilities that generic UI automation cannot reproduce comparably.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes shared log, role-specific approval links, per-agent computers, and same computer_run tool for agent and person.
Manager approval adds tools to every browser without reload.
Ablation claims 0/8 shipped with engine versus 8/8 without it.
execution_rationale: The 173-second video, transcript, frame sheets, live demo, and extensive claimed tests present unusually complete evidence of a coherent multi-user system; some claims remain self-reported.
execution_evidence: 173-second submitted video with transcript and three frame sheets.
Transcript walks through rooms, logs, computers, draft/publish approval, and tool propagation.
About text reports 23/23 clean-Chrome tests and an ablation.
impact_rationale: Teams using autonomous agents have a concrete need for isolation, auditability, human approval, and shared operational visibility; the system addresses the failure modes directly.
impact_evidence: Multiple-agent rooms and role-based approval target real collaborative workflows.
Failure signals, shared logs, and publish gating are demonstrated/claimed.
creativity_rationale: Git-for-agent-work with a computer per agent and every call as a commit is a memorable, ambitious interaction and infrastructure model pursued deeply.
creativity_evidence: Distinct room/commit/computer abstraction.
Cross-agent tool borrowing and human approval are integrated rather than ornamental.
usability_note: The demo is designed for one-click entry, but the multi-role and credential model introduces inherent complexity.
red_flags: Some quantitative claims are self-reported rather than independently verified.
Per-agent computer isolation and credential handling merit security scrutiny.
standouts: Human approval is enforced as a system primitive.
advance_reason: Most complete and ambitious packet, with transformative WebMCP leverage and strong demonstrated workflow.

one_line: Evidence-dated food rule verification for agents, using explicit verdicts instead of unsafe certainty.
what_it_does: Turns household constraints into typed rules and checks products, menus, or meal plans against dated nutrition/allergen evidence, returning four verdicts and optional records.
leverage_rationale: The structured page state preserves typed household rules, source/date evidence, refusal semantics, and auditable verdicts in a form an agent can use reliably; generic UI driving loses much of this safety structure.
leverage_evidence: Four verdicts include honest unknown states and never use 'safe'.
Sources and dates attach to evidence; unknown counts as no.
About text reports measured browser-agent and direct-API comparisons.
execution_rationale: The product concept, evidence model, and safety language are unusually coherent; frame sheets show ruled answers and evidence-oriented screens, though no transcript confirms end-to-end interactions.
execution_evidence: Three video frame sheets show ruled answer/source/date and refusal states.
Specific Kroger broth case identifies 780 mg sodium and dated conflict.
Demo and public repository are reported alive.
impact_rationale: Families managing allergies or dietary limits face a high-stakes, specific problem, and the product directly addresses the danger of unsupported AI food-safety claims.
impact_evidence: Milk-allergic child and sodium-limit scenario are concrete.
Product/menu/meal-plan verification and permanent records fit caregivers, schools, and kitchens.
creativity_rationale: Replacing the culturally dangerous binary 'safe' answer with dated evidence and principled unknown verdicts is a novel interaction and communication model.
creativity_evidence: Never-safe framing and refusal as a valid answer.
Typed household rules plus dated source-backed records.
usability_note: Explicit verdicts and visible evidence support careful decisions, though the domain requires users to understand unknown/no semantics.
red_flags: Food safety remains dependent on source freshness and completeness.
No transcript and no independent validation of the measured comparisons.
standouts: Strong evidence honesty and safety semantics.
advance_reason: High-impact, creative, and safety-conscious use of structured agent evidence.

one_line: An agent and learner grow a personal knowledge map branch by branch.
what_it_does: Excalidraw-based canvas exposes map, selection, and questions to ChatGPT; the agent researches and adds a few nodes while the learner edits, pins questions, and writes notes.
leverage_rationale: Shared live canvas state and a recomputed how_to_use guide let the agent collaborate precisely without screenshots, while intentionally stopping for learner direction.
leverage_evidence: 17 tools expose live map, selection, and open questions.
Agent is instructed to draw a few nodes, stop, and wait for the person.
Agent can refuse when there is no room rather than overwrite work.
execution_rationale: The interaction model is coherent and frame sheets show a map/canvas progression, but there is no transcript or repository execution trace in the packet and end-to-end research is only partially evidenced.
execution_evidence: Three video frame sheets show Study Map canvas states.
Live link and public repository are listed.
About text identifies an MIT retrofit of Excalidraw.
impact_rationale: Learners who retain knowledge better through active, personalized mapping have a clear desire addressed by incremental co-construction rather than passive generated summaries.
impact_evidence: Specific learner pain point: finished maps are read once and forgotten.
Learner owns notes, selection, and branch growth.
creativity_rationale: The stop-and-wait, curiosity-driven map growth is a notably original interaction model for agent-assisted learning.
creativity_evidence: how_to_use is recomputed from live canvas and teaches the agent pacing.
Agent and learner share one editable canvas with distinct roles.
usability_note: Incremental growth and explicit learner control are promising, though canvas density may become challenging as maps grow.
red_flags: Built as an MIT retrofit of existing Excalidraw.
No transcript; agent calls are inferred from frame sequence/about text.
standouts: Excellent pedagogical pacing encoded in the tool surface.
advance_reason: Original learning interaction with strong WebMCP-specific shared-state design.

one_line: Browser-local zero-knowledge pharmacogenomic checks that reveal a proof, not raw DNA.
what_it_does: Parses genetic files locally and uses Groth16 zk-SNARKs to let an agent obtain proof of a drug contraindication without receiving the genome.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP bridges an agent to a privacy-preserving local computation whose raw input must not enter agent context; this is a capability general UI automation or server MCP cannot safely replicate.
leverage_evidence: Core claim is that the agent operates the browser without receiving any DNA letters.
Groth16 proof and browser trust boundary are central to the product.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
execution_rationale: The architecture and scope are coherent, but no video frame sheets were submitted and the packet does not visibly prove parsing, proof generation, or verification end-to-end.
execution_evidence: No video frame sheets submitted.
Seven gallery images are listed and Devpost screenshot is packaging evidence only.
About text claims full raw-file parsing and in-browser proof workflow.
impact_rationale: Protecting genetic privacy while enabling clinically relevant contraindication checks addresses a high-stakes, real need for patients and medical agents.
impact_evidence: Concrete Plavix pharmacogenomic scenario and fatal-clot risk are described.
Pattern is framed for other sensitive medical and financial data.
creativity_rationale: Combining WebMCP with zero-knowledge proofs for agent-accessible genomic safety is highly novel and ambitious, with a clear conceptual reframing of the browser as trust boundary.
creativity_evidence: Zero-knowledge proof rather than raw-data disclosure.
Highest-stakes dataset used to demonstrate a general privacy pattern.
usability_note: The safety goal is clear, but genomic upload/proof workflows are technically demanding and unobserved in this packet.
red_flags: No video evidence.
Clinical correctness and cryptographic circuit coverage require deeper validation.
High-stakes claims are primarily self-reported.
standouts: WebMCP is structurally necessary, not decorative.
advance_reason: Outstanding concept and leverage, despite execution confidence being capped by absent video evidence.

one_line: Agent-driven live DNS, TLS, mail, and crawler diagnostics rendered as inspectable evidence.
what_it_does: Runs live network diagnostic commands and an agent-planned investigation, rendering each result on the page as a case file rather than returning only a summary.
leverage_rationale: Live structured lookups and persistent on-page evidence materially improve freshness, transparency, and repeatability over a general agent clicking a terminal-like UI; the diagnostics themselves remain possible elsewhere.
leverage_evidence: 27 registered tools span DNS, TLS, RDAP, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, ASN/routing, and crawler readability.
dug_investigate accepts an agent-written ordered command list and files each result.
Screenshot visibly shows an agent-asked TLS command and certificate evidence timeline.
execution_rationale: The screenshot and frame evidence show a coherent terminal/evidence workflow, and the live demo is reported alive; the packet lacks a transcript, so breadth of all 27 tools is not fully verified.
execution_evidence: Three video frame sheets are submitted.
Screenshot visibly shows TLS 1.3, issuer, validity, and an ASKED BY YOUR AGENT state.
Demo and public repository are reported alive.
impact_rationale: Domain owners, mail operators, and developers have a real need for current, inspectable diagnostics instead of stale model explanations or opaque summaries.
impact_evidence: Concrete spam-delivery troubleshooting scenario.
Per-result case file preserves SPF tree and other evidence for inspection.
creativity_rationale: Turning agent-planned live diagnostics into a visible case file, including a browser-only tool, is a fresh and well-focused interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent supplies ordered investigative steps.
Results render progressively on the same page rather than disappearing into context.
usability_note: Command-oriented interface is transparent for technical users; breadth may be intimidating for non-specialists.
red_flags: No transcript; some breadth claims are not individually demonstrated.
Live network results can vary with target and time.
standouts: Agent-planned investigation is more than a tool list.
advance_reason: Strong visual evidence, clear audience value, and a substantial structured-agent delta.
